findings.title: AI-review caller pins a SHA but the reusable workflow executes reviewer code from mutable main with all repository secrets
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/ai-review.yml:25 pins MaineCyberTech/ai-reviewer/.github/workflows/ai-review.yml@d401040c9777a63195396cbf177eec78192284d2, but that workflow checks the reviewer repository out at `ref: main` (MaineCyberTech/ai-reviewer@d401040c:.github/workflows/ai-review.yml:58-64) and then executes .ai-reviewer/.github/scripts/ai_review.py and the prompt from that checkout (:83-87). ai-reviewer main advanced from d401040c (2026-11-06T17:03Z) to 80872e5 (2026-11-06T19:32Z), so the pin does not control the executed code. The caller also passes `secrets: inherit` (.github/workflows/ai-review.yml:26), making every repository secret - not just AI_REVIEW_ENDPOINT/AI_REVIEW_API_KEY/AI_REVIEW_MODEL (AGENTS.md:109-111) - available to that mutable checkout.
findings.remediation: Checkout the reviewer at the same 40-character SHA (or vendor the script/prompt in this repo) instead of `ref: main`, and pass only the three AI_REVIEW_* secrets explicitly instead of `secrets: inherit`. Re-pin and review the new SHA in the PR that updates it.

findings.title: Bot approval fails open when `gh pr checks --required` errors, approving without verified required checks
findings.evidence: MaineCyberTech/ai-reviewer@d401040c:.github/workflows/bot-approval.yml:61-81: both the wait loop (:62) and the final gate (:76) run `checks="$(gh pr checks "$PR" --required --json name,state)" || checks='[]'`; on any command failure (API/rate limit, auth, or no resolvable required contexts) checks becomes [] and pending is 0, and the workflow proceeds to POST /repos/$REPO/pulls/$PR/reviews with event=APPROVE (:83-85). The caller grants the needed token at .github/workflows/bot-approval.yml:9-12. The control is therefore fail-open exactly when the check query is untrustworthy.
findings.remediation: Treat a non-zero `gh pr checks` exit, empty output or unparsable JSON as a hard refusal; require a non-empty set of required contexts for the protected branch and only approve after a fresh successful query.

findings.title: Dependabot Node-major hold is applied only to the root docker config, not the three app Dockerfile directories
findings.evidence: .github/dependabot.yml:55-59 ignores `node` semver-major updates only for directory "/", while the separate docker entries for /apps/api (:64-72), /apps/web (:74-82) and /apps/worker (:84-92) have no ignore block. The held Node 25/26 majors in issue #361 were exactly those directories (closed PRs #266 /apps/api, #268 /apps/web, #269 /apps/worker), and all three Dockerfiles still start FROM node:20-alpine (apps/api/Dockerfile:1, apps/web/Dockerfile:1, apps/worker/Dockerfile:1). Dependabot will recreate those major PRs on the next weekly run.
findings.remediation: Add the same `dependency-name: node` / `version-update:semver-major` ignore to each app docker entry (or fold them into a single config if Dependabot supports the layout) and keep the #361 table in sync.

findings.title: AI review fails on Dependabot PRs because required secrets are unavailable, creating red checks and blocking the bot-approval path
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/ai-review.yml:5-7 triggers on every pull_request, including Dependabot. The callee declares AI_REVIEW_ENDPOINT and AI_REVIEW_API_KEY as required (MaineCyberTech/ai-reviewer@d401040c:.github/workflows/ai-review.yml:16-22) and exits when they are empty (:75-78), but Dependabot-triggered runs do not receive repository Actions secrets. Observed 2026-11-07: ai-review run 42346875347 for Dependabot PR #379 failed with the workflow annotation 'Secret AI_REVIEW_ENDPOINT is required, but not provided while calling' and 'Secret AI_REVIEW_API_KEY is required, but not provided while calling'; run 42346888919 (PR #382) also failed and runs 42346879642/42346884197 were cancelled. No AI-review comment was posted on #379-#382, so bot-approval (which requires that comment) cannot approve any of them.
findings.remediation: Skip Dependabot (and fork) PRs at the caller job level, or add the AI_REVIEW_* values as Dependabot secrets. If the review is truly advisory, treat missing secrets as a skipped job rather than a red check.

findings.title: Bot approval accepts any historical AI-review comment, so a review from an earlier push can satisfy the gate
findings.evidence: MaineCyberTech/ai-reviewer@d401040c:.github/workflows/bot-approval.yml:54-59 only checks that some comment by github-actions[bot] contains 'AI review (advisory)'; it does not compare the comment's commit or time to the current PR head, and it does not require the latest ai-review run to have succeeded. The caller now triggers on synchronize (.github/workflows/ai-review.yml:7), so a failed or cancelled review on the latest push leaves the previous comment in place and the approval gate still passes. No current exploit was observed, but the gate proves a review exists, not that it covers the approved SHA.
findings.remediation: Have ai-review include the head SHA in the comment and have bot-approval require the parsed SHA to equal the PR head and the latest ai-review check to be green before approving.

findings.title: tailwind-merge 3.x is installed against Tailwind CSS 3.4, so class-conflict merging uses Tailwind v4 semantics
findings.evidence: packages/ui/package.json:32 and apps/web/package.json:32 declare tailwind-merge ^3.7.0 while apps/web/package.json:54 keeps tailwindcss ^3.4.19; packages/ui/src/lib/cn.ts:5 calls twMerge for all shared components. The tailwind-merge v3.7.0 README states 'Supports Tailwind v4.0 up to v4.3 (if you use Tailwind v3, use tailwind-merge v2.6.0)'. Reproduced with the 3.7.0 bundle: twMerge('outline-none','outline') returns both classes, and the shadow/rounded class renames mean merged output semantics differ from Tailwind 3.
findings.remediation: Pin tailwind-merge to 2.6.x while Tailwind remains on v3, or complete the Tailwind v4 migration before keeping tailwind-merge 3.x. Add a cn() unit fixture covering the v3 override names.
